record.final_answer:
Yes — but not by tuning the poll interval. That door is closed.

What the Nimbrel SDK docs say (server SDK 4.x, read 2026-04-20, docs.nimbrel.example/sdk/updates — the example host doesn't resolve from here, so this is from the stored read, not a fresh check):

  - Default propagation is polling every 30 seconds.
  - The polling interval cannot be configured below 10 seconds.
  - Push updates require stream: true in the client options, and are gated to the Team plan or above.

So the 10-second floor sits above your 5-second target. Any service that stays on polling is structurally out of spec, no matter what config you set — best case there is ~10s, worst case 30s.

That leaves the push path. With streaming you're in "event delivered on change" territory, which generally lands well inside 5s. It's achievable, but it's a real piece of work, not a toggle:

  1. Enable it per service, in code — every service's SDK client needs stream: true. That's a config change plus a redeploy of each one, not something the console flips for you.
  2. Confirm the plan. Stream is Team-and-above. If the account is on a lower tier, this is a commercial prerequisite, not an engineering one — worth checking before anyone commits to the 5s SLA.
  3. Handle the connection lifecycle. A stream is a long-lived connection: reconnect with backoff, a resync-on-reconnect so you don't miss the change that happened during the gap, and a slow fallback poll so a silently dropped stream doesn't leave a service serving stale flag values forever. That "stream died quietly" failure mode is the one that bites in production.
  4. Check the network path. Long-lived streaming HTTP doesn't always survive ingress: load balancer idle timeouts, proxy buffering, and read timeouts will each kill a stream that looks healthy from the app side.
  5. Measure the right thing. Verify console-flip-to-flag-change end to end, not "stream connected". A connected stream that isn't being applied is the failure you won't see otherwise.

One caveat on scope: /stand/ws is an empty repo (single empty "initial" commit, no files), so I can't inspect your services, SDK versions, or how they're deployed. I also don't know your current Nimbrel plan. Items 1 and 2 are the ones that decide whether this is a config change or a project — tell me the SDK version per service and the plan tier and I can be specific.
